Need to search first.I don't have any notes for Job 18 yet. My research tools stopped working before I could read a single page.

- My first try at opening eight commentary pages at once (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Barnes, Precept Austin, Matthew Henry and Benson) hit a tool usage limit, so none of them loaded.
- My next try at opening the Enduring Word page was refused because the tool only opens links that first came up in a search.
- When I ran that search, I'd used up all my tool calls for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I won't write verse notes from memory.

If you ask again in a new message, my tool limits should reset. I'll search first and then open only a few pages at a time, in this order:
1. **Verse by verse:** Enduring Word's Job 18 page, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on biblehub.com, and Precept Austin's Job 18 page.
2. **Where traditions differ:** Wesley's Notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Matthew Henry, and anything on Job 18 at ligonier.org, gty.org, desiringgod.org or 1517.org. Bildad's claim that the wicked always suffer in this life (vv. 5–21) is the most likely place for a real difference.
3. **Other views:** netbible.org notes, especially on "the firstborn of death" (v. 13) and "the king of terrors" (v. 14), plus bibleodyssey.org, and Catholic and Orthodox readings (for example, Gregory the Great's *Moralia* on ccel.org or newadvent.org). I'll also check gotquestions.org for teaching that links Bildad's argument to the prosperity gospel.

As you asked, every point will have its URL, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
